text: Good evening, Mr Mayor and Councillors. I note in the recommendations of the report in front of you is the endorsement of a community room in the proposed facility for Boronia Park. I strongly believe that this is an absolutely critical part of the proposed building, offering a space that supports sporting clubs and that they have been asking for for more than 40 years. Although we exist to promote our sports, the importance of sporting clubs to the social fabric of our communities cannot be overstated. They provide touchpoints for people across our community, promoting interaction and engagement. We have over 500 playing members of our club, the vast majority being kids under 16. But the real number of engaged members of our sporting club community spread way beyond this. Parents, friends, supporters and our extensive ex-player network all bring life and vibrancy to the club. At Huntsville Rugby, we are very proud of the fact that we are a cradle-to-grave club, providing opportunity to stay engaged from age 4 to 84. It is the intergenerational support that this approach provides that keeps our club strong. Many of our older members have been involved for well over 50 years. And although I probably shouldn't be telling Council this, the ashes of a number of past members have been spread on this sacred Boronia Park. This place means that much to us. Success for sporting clubs is often measured by the number of trophies in the cabinet. But winning football matches is not the main thing most people get out of our club. Over a glass of wine on a Friday evening, watching the under-10s strut their stuff, while turning sausages on the barbie on a Saturday afternoon, or while cheering on the famous black and white hoops from the sidelines, relationships, friendships form. Relationships that are critical to each individual, but also for the creation of strong communities. Over the years, we have been forced to have these experiences outdoors, subjected to the weather conditions of the day. There is no doubt this has hampered our efforts to bring people into the Hunters Hill family. The impacts of social isolation have been highlighted over the past year by the pandemic. It is critical that we have spaces that provide more opportunities for social inclusion and engagement. But this space at Boronia Park needs to be fit for purpose. It needs to allow enough space to support our AGMs and our committee meetings, hold referee training and coaching courses, put on simple family dinners to support our parents, hold our fundraising season launch, or our end-of-season awards. Of course, it needs to allow our members to engage and socialise with each other. These are the things that are critical to the operation and continued success of our community sporting clubs. We only get one chance to get this right for now and the generations to come. Thank you. Chair Perks.

text: Thank you. Good evening, Mayor, Ross Williams and Councillors. As Ross has said, I'm Carole Sheldrake and I'm also the President of the Huntersville Bridge Club. The Bridge Club is a large community group within Huntersville with over 340 members and we are still growing. It's a volunteer-run, not-for-profit organisation with a reputation as a very professionally run bridge club. The club has been part of the Huntersville community for nearly 50 years and during this period we have had a longstanding and continuous association with the Huntersville Council. We've been at the Henley Bowling Club for nearly 11 years with a sole occupancy agreement for Monday to Friday usage since 2012. At no time have we had any usage over the weekends. During this period, we've paid Council a significant yearly rental, as noted in the paper before you, of $34,000 a year in 2021. The Huntersville Bridge Club contributes significantly to the fabric of the local community through its operation. It provides a fantastic social amenity through social interactions for members and contributes immensely to the good mental health and individual wellbeing of members. All players are welcome to participate at club sessions. It's open to all. Our problem is now in terms of the licence. We have been in discussion with Council officers over the last months on the key terms of our licence. In recent weeks, it appears that there has been a significant shift to the original negotiated agreement. Firstly, Council agreed that the bridge club would have accessible storage for our equipment to enable the regular pack-up and set-up should Council rent out the hall to other users during the week. We've now learned that Council plans to demolish the small room near the kitchen to enlarge the hall. There is no plan at the moment to replace this with alternate accessible storage. This loss of accessible storage will affect our ability to operate on a daily basis. Secondly, the recent advice that Council will undertake significant works at the Henley Bowling Club without any reference to Council providing the club with alternate appropriately sized accessible accommodation if the hall is not available. Thirdly, the negotiated discussion was that Council will give the club reasonable advance notice if pack-up is required midweek or at the weekend. This is not noted in the present licence terms. Finally, we are aware that, at present, Council can only negotiate a one-year lease, but there is a lack of mention of the opportunity for ongoing tenure in 2022. The club prepares its yearly program in October for the following year and needs some security for 2022. Therefore, for the club, the issues are the need for accessible storage to enable the club to manage the usage of the venue by other users midweek, a guarantee of Council providing suitably sized alternate venues if the hall is not available for the club due to Council undertaking work as listed in the document at the site. Thirdly, an inclusion in the terms that Council will give the club reasonable advance notice for pack-up if the room is leased out to other users midweek. Finally, the offer of ongoing security of tenure for 2022 and onwards. Thank you for your time and the opportunity to address Council. Thank you.
